# Research notes: Newsom special session on AI before Jan 1, 2027 (as of 2026-10-05)

**Bottom line:** As of Oct 5, 2026, no proclamation has been issued, so the question has not resolved. Newsom has openly floated an AI special session since Sept 17, and agency recommendations are due Nov 16. Newsom has never called a session on AI, no legislative leader has backed one publicly, and his leverage as a lame duck is weak.

## 1. Resolution sources

**California Constitution, Art. IV, Sec. 3(b)** ([leginfo](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CONS&sectionNum=SEC.%203.&article=IV), fetched 2026-10-05):
> "On extraordinary occasions the Governor by proclamation may cause the Legislature to assemble in special session. When so assembled it has power to legislate only on subjects specified in the proclamation but may provide for expenses and other matters incidental to the session."

**Key dates from the constitution:**
- Sec. 3(a): the regular session adjourns sine die at midnight on Nov 30, 2026.
- The new Legislature convenes the first Monday of December, which I calculate as Dec 7, 2026 (not confirmed by a published calendar).
- Newsom's term ends in early January 2027, probably Jan 4 (inferred from Art. V; not confirmed).

**gov.ca.gov, checked 2026-10-05:**
- No special-session proclamation has been posted since Sept 30.
- The latest items in the Proclamations category are commemorative: Sept 30 (Indian Boarding Schools remembrance day), Sept 25, Sept 18 and Sept 17.
- The Newsroom from Sept 30 to Oct 5 has only bill signings, an AI worker-protections release, appointments, CARE Court and an economy release.
- *Uncertain:* the category page shows only the latest five items.

**[Metaculus Q45820](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/45820):** the page returned HTTP 403, so I could not see its background or community forecast.

**Status:** not resolved. No AI special-session proclamation exists as of 2026-10-05.

## 2. Recent news and status quo

**Newsom's statements and actions:**
- **2026-09-17, Politico interview:** Newsom floated an AI special session.
  - "Is there a legislative play? Is there a framework around a special session in that respect? Is there executive action?"
  - "...what we can do in the next few weeks — days, weeks, and months."
  - He cited a July 2026 incident where "rogue OpenAI programs executed an autonomous cyberattack," and federal inaction.
  - He called the AI bills he had signed "the floor, not the ceiling."
  - Sources: [Yahoo/Politico](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/newsom-floats-prospect-special-session-172500672.html), [SacBee via Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/gov-gavin-newsom-mulls-further-190449509.html).
- **2026-09-18, AI safety executive order:**
  - It directs the Government Operations Agency and the Office of Emergency Services to deliver recommendations by **Nov 16, 2026**.
  - Topics: outside safety evaluators, independent verification of safety frameworks, "kill switches," and reporting of loss-of-control incidents.
  - CalMatters says the recommendations "could form the basis of a special legislative session." Sen. Wiener: "We must act with all possible haste."
  - Sources: [CalMatters](https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/09/ai-rules-newsom-state-directive/), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/california-gavin-newsom-ai-order-safety-regulations-kill-switch-rcna598570).
- **2026-09-30, last day to act on bills:**
  - He signed about 11–12 more AI safety bills, roughly 30 AI measures for the year ([Transparency Coalition](https://www.transparencycoalition.ai/news/gov-newsom-wraps-california-term-by-enacting-11-more-laws-on-ai-safety)).
  - At a news conference he "left open the possibility" of an AI special session: "We have to do a lot more in the absence of federal leadership" ([ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/california-gov-gavin-newsom-signs-laws-protect-workers-136904967)).
  - *Uncertain:* a search snippet says he is "contemplating" a session to put the kill switch into law. The SF Chronicle article it came from would not load.
- **2026-10-01:** "I'm going to be stubborn to the last day. And that is keeping my options open with these special sessions." He did not name AI specifically ([CBS Sacramento](https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/newsom-final-legislative-session-california-governor/)).
- **2026-10-02:**
  - The Transparency Coalition update mentions no planned special session and expects no more California AI bills "until early next year" ([link](https://www.transparencycoalition.ai/news/ai-legislative-update-october2-2026)).
  - KP Public Affairs says he "hinted at" a fall wildfire session, but Senate participation is unclear ([link](https://www.kppublicaffairs.com/kpinsights/2026-legislative-session-closeout-report)).

**Competing topic: wildfire liability.**
- **2026-09-02:** the SB 492 wildfire-liability deal collapsed. Speaker Rivas had opposed it ("half measures"). Newsom refused to rule out a special session ([CalMatters](https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/09/newsom-lame-duck-session/)).
- **2026-09-30:** he sounded pessimistic about that session: "I'm not naive about how difficult that was" ([Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/newsom-says-deal-utilities-wildfire-234138665.html)).
- A wildfire session could later be amended to add AI, which would count for YES under the fine print.

**Leaders and leverage:**
- I found no public position from Speaker Rivas or Senate Pro Tem Limón on an AI session.
- Newsom is widely described as a weakened lame duck, especially with the Assembly.
- Coverage ties his AI turn to 2028 presidential positioning ([meaww](https://news.meaww.com/kill-switch-returns-to-ai-debate-as-newsom-raises-2028-stakes-in-tech-fight-with-trump); lower-quality source).

**Federal context:**
- Trump signed an executive order on state AI laws on 2025-12-11.
- DOJ's AI Litigation Task Force was set up around 2026-01-09.
- I found no confirmed DOJ lawsuit against a California AI law. One source says no California AI law had been blocked as of Jul 2026 (*uncertain*).

**Prediction markets:** as of 2026-10-05, searches found no related market on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold. I did not browse those sites directly.

**Scheduled dates:**

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Nov 16, 2026 | AI recommendations due under the Sept 18 order |
| Nov 30, 2026 | Regular session ends |
| ~Dec 7, 2026 | New Legislature convenes |
| ~Jan 4, 2027 | Newsom's term ends |

## 3. Base rates

**Newsom's special sessions** (four sessions, five proclamations):

| Proclaimed | Convened | Topic | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nov 30, 2022 (announced ~Sept 30, 2022) | Dec 5, 2022, the December organizational day | Oil price gouging | [gov.ca.gov](https://www.gov.ca.gov/2022/11/30/governor-newsom-convenes-special-session-to-hold-oil-industry-accountable-for-price-gouging-keep-money-in-californians-pockets/) |
| Aug 31, 2024, last night of the regular session | Immediately, alongside the regular session | Refinery fuel inventories | [gov.ca.gov](https://www.gov.ca.gov/2024/08/31/gas-price-special-session/) |
| Nov 7, 2024, lame-duck window | Dec 2, 2024, the December organizational day | Litigation funds against the federal government | [Senate weekly history](https://www.senate.ca.gov/system/files/2024-12/swh-12-20-2024-1x.pdf) |
| Jan 13, 2025 (amendment) | — | Added LA fire funding | [proclamation PDF](https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Special-Session-Amend-Proc-1-13-25-1402hrs.pdf) |

- The 2025 redistricting package passed in the regular session, not a special session.
- I found no 2020 COVID special session (only partly verified).
- None of Newsom's sessions has ever included AI.

**Pattern:**
- Two of the four sessions were proclaimed in Nov of an election year and convened on the December organizational day, matching the window this question covers.
- He has never proclaimed one in October.
- Frequency has risen since late 2022.
- The California Budget Center says special sessions happened in about half of the last 26 legislative cycles ([link](https://calbudgetcenter.org/resources/understanding-special-sessions-in-california/), Aug 2025).

**Other states with AI in a special session:**
- **Colorado:** Gov. Polis called a session on 2025-08-06. It included delaying the state AI Act, which SB 4 did on 2025-08-26 ([Colorado Sun](https://coloradosun.com/2025/08/06/colorado-special-session-big-beautiful-bill/)).
- **Florida:** around 2026-04-15, Gov. DeSantis added an "AI Bill of Rights" to his redistricting session. The House killed it on 2026-04-28 ([Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/04/15/desantis-delays-redistricting-special-session-expands-it-to-ai-vaccines/)).
- In both cases AI was an add-on to a session called mainly for something else. I found no governor who has called a session solely on AI (search not exhaustive).

**Pre-opening flag:** Newsom's statements of Sept 17–30 and the Sept 18 order all came before the question opened on 2026-09-30. Only a proclamation issued after Sept 30, 2026 counts, and none has been found.

criterios:
This question resolves as **Yes** if, after September 30, 2026 and before January 1, 2027, California Governor Gavin Newsom issues a proclamation convening the California Legislature in special session (also called extraordinary session) whose subject specified in the proclamation pursuant to [Article IV, Section 3(b)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CONS\&sectionNum=SEC.%203.\&article=IV) of the California Constitution, is artificial intelligence, AI safety, AI oversight, or a substantially equivalent subject.

This question resolves as **No** if this event does not occur.

Resolution will be determined by the proclamation as published by the Governor's office at gov.ca.gov, the California Legislative Information site (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), or the Assembly or Senate Daily Journal.
letra_pequena:
* This question also resolves as **Yes** if Governor Newsom amends or supplements a special session proclamation to revise the topics addressed to include artificial intelligence, AI safety, AI oversight, or a substantially equivalent subject. 
* Only the issuance of the proclamation matters. Whether the session convenes, how long it lasts, and whether any legislation passes do not affect resolution.
* AI need not be the sole subject. A proclamation covering multiple topics resolves YES if AI is among the stated purposes.
* A special session running concurrently with the regular session that convenes in December 2026 counts, provided a proclamation is issued.
* If a proclamation is issued on or before December 31, 2026 for a session convening in 2027, this resolves YES.
* If Newsom leaves office before December 31, 2026, a proclamation by his successor or an acting Governor does **not** count.

(d) **No scenario:** The November 16 recommendations arrive, and Newsom pursues executive or agency action rather than proclaiming a special session.

(a) **Time left:** About 12 weeks remain, until December 31, 2026. The likeliest window for any proclamation is mid-November to early December. That follows the November 16 agency recommendations and the new Legislature convening around December 7.

(b) **Status quo:** No proclamation has been issued. If nothing changes, this resolves No.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:**
- Newsom has issued special-session proclamations in about four of roughly eight late-year windows.
- He has used the November lame-duck window twice: November 2022 (oil price gouging) and November 2024 (litigation funds).
- None of his sessions has included AI.
- Across governors, AI has only ever appeared as an add-on to a session called mainly for something else (Colorado, Florida).
- When a governor has publicly floated a special session on a specific topic, he fairly often follows through, perhaps 30–50% of the time. Lame-duck status and no backing from legislative leaders pull that down.

(d) **No scenario:** The November 16 recommendations arrive, and Newsom chooses executive action and agency rulemaking, such as verification requirements implemented through Cal OES. Speaker Rivas and Senate Pro Tem Limón signal that a session would simply gavel in and out. A session convening December 7 would mostly outlast Newsom's term, leaving his successor to sign any bills. So he leaves the package for the 2027 regular session. The wildfire session also doesn't materialize.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Newsom wants a closing national headline before a 2028 run. After the November 16 report, he issues a proclamation in late November covering kill-switch and independent-verification legislation, convening alongside the December 7 organizational session. This mirrors his 2022 and 2024 pattern, and Senator Wiener champions it. Alternatively, he calls a wildfire session and folds AI into it.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- Only the issuance of the proclamation matters, so a symbolic proclamation counts even if the Legislature ignores it.
- An amendment to any special session that adds AI also counts.
- A proclamation issued in December for a session convening in 2027 counts.
- Because only issuance matters, the bar is lower than "a special session happens."
- On the other side, Newsom has many non-session options and openly listed them as alternatives.

His repeated "keeping my options open" rhetoric and the cheapness of a proclamation support Yes. Weak leverage, no stated leadership support, and the fact that a December session would mostly fall to his successor push toward No.

Probability: 30%
